_about: Provenance of the 50 sages added from Shem HaGedolim (ids 630-679) and the owner's own material, generated from the validated fragments of the content packages (scratchpad shg-work). Per sage: the Maarekhet Sefarim entry that names him or his book (shg: ref, verbatim quote, the words by which the Chida names him), the sources read for his bio and core idea with the verbatim quotes that support each sentence, the links with their quotes, and the worker's notes on disagreeing sources and what was left out. A reserve sage replaced a planned one that has no entry in Maarekhet Sefarim. Never hand-edit; tests/shemHagedolim.test.ts fails when an id now belongs to another sage.

sages.notes: Years: sources disagree. Hebrew Wikipedia: born ה׳רס״ז (1506/1507), died 13 Nisan ש״ס (1600). Sefaria: 1507 (birth approximate) - 1600. The owner's paper and English Wikipedia: born 1508; English Wikipedia and the Mahariit (per the paper) put his death in 1593, while the gravestone date given by the paper and Hebrew Wikipedia is 13 Nisan 1600. Written as כ־1507–1600 (the dates two independent catalogues agree on, birth marked approximate); the bio and core idea carry no year. Left out of the bio on purpose: the story of the son who was taken or converted (told only in tradition, English Wikipedia says "legend has it"), the Ari's refusal to teach him Kabbalah (a tradition, Hebrew Wikipedia says "ישנה מסורת"). Kabbalah in his commentaries: English Wikipedia (Jewish Encyclopedia 1906) says his works "rarely betray any traces of the Kabbalah", the owner's paper describes a synthesis of peshat, remez, derash and sod with kabbalistic ideas in homiletic dress: the core idea therefore says only what both agree on (questions first, a moral lesson from every verse). Relations seen, not recorded as links: semikha from Karo after Berab's renewal (not a teaching relation); ordained Yom Tov Tzahalon, taught Yitzchak Trivus (neither on the roster); his son Chaim Alshich (not on the roster); close to the Ramak and honoured by the Ari per the paper (no source states a teacher-student relation); the Alshich as a disciple of Taitazak is recorded as a teacher link to id 68 (the roster spells his name טאיטצאק, Hebrew Wikipedia טאיטאצאק, hence the validator's name warning). The MS entry used (Mem 219:1) is one of several that name him: Mem 3:1 (Meah Shearim, lost), Resh 10 (Rav Peninim), Resh 17 (Romemot El), Chet 26 (Chavatzelet HaSharon, Shoshanat HaAmakim).

sages.notes: Years: Hebrew Wikipedia, English Wikipedia and Sefaria all give 1545 (born in Safed) - 1604; the owner's paper says he died 1604-1605 (ה׳שס״ד-ה׳שס״ה). Written 1545–1604. The mission to Constantinople is dated ה׳שנ״ז (1597) by the paper; the bio gives no year for it. Printing: Hebrew Wikipedia says Midrash Shmuel was first printed in Venice in של״ט (1579); English Wikipedia lists Venice 1579, 1585, 1597. Not recorded as links (not teacher/family/influence, or the other man is not on the roster): friendship with Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (the Ramak, id 71; Hebrew and English Wikipedia and the paper call him his friend), the fellow-disciple relation with the Alshich (id 630, whom Hebrew Wikipedia calls "another disciple of the Ari" and the paper "his friend"; a source for the Alshich being the Ari's disciple appears only here, so the Alshich record does not claim it), his teacher Rabbi Elisha Galico (not on the roster). The paper's claims that the Ari said Uceda carried the soul of R. Pinchas ben Yair and that he signed first on the 1575 deed are not used. The Hebrew bio names the Ari 1534–1572 (id 462) as teacher on Hebrew Wikipedia's "מתלמידיו הראשונים של האר״י" and Sefaria "a disciple of the Arizal and R. Chaim Vital". Namesake note: the Midrash Shmuel of Rabbi Shmuel de Uzeda on Avot is not the early aggadic Midrash Shmuel on the Book of Samuel (the paper makes the same distinction).

sages.notes: Years: Hebrew Wikipedia gives 1500 (ה׳ר״ס) - 1580 (ניסן ה׳ש״ם, "או ה׳שמ״ה" for the year of death); Sefaria gives 1505 (Salonica) - 1585. Written כ־1500–1580, the Hebrew Wikipedia dates. The bio has no year. Length of service: Hebrew Wikipedia says he sat in the Safed court 54 years, Sefaria says he was the community's rabbi for 55 years, so the bio says more than fifty. Not recorded as links: friendship with Rabbi Yosef Karo (id 443: colleague; Hebrew Wikipedia says both were ordained together by Berab), contact with the Alshich (id 630), the Radbaz and others; his teachers Rabbi Yosef Fasi and his uncle Rabbi Aharon of Trani (not on the roster); the Rid of Trani is only a family ancestor in the sources ("משפחה שהתייחסה לרבי ישעיה דיטראני"), not recorded. Origin of the family: Hebrew Wikipedia calls it a family of exiles from Spain, English Wikipedia (Jewish Encyclopedia) says his father fled to Salonica from Apulia, so the bio says only that he was born in Salonica. Age at aliyah: 18 in Hebrew Wikipedia, 16 in English Wikipedia, not stated. Namesake: the Mabit (Moshe ben Yosef, Safed, 16th century) is not the Rid or the Riaz of Trani (ids 308, 403, Italy, 13th century) and not Rabbi Moshe of Trani's son Rabbi Yosef of Trani (the Maharit, planned id 641, family link recorded 632 to 641 with the Hebrew Wikipedia sentence about his two sons). The Mabit's Beit Elohim is not Rabbi Bachya's or any other book of the same name. MS: Kof 112:1 (Kiryat Sefer) and Bet 44:1 (Beit Elohim) both name him by his epithet המבי״ט. Note: Maarekhet Sefarim Kof 111:1 is a different Kiryat Sefer (by the Meiri).

sages.notes: Years: Hebrew Wikipedia gives "סביב ה׳י׳ 1250 - ה׳ע׳ 1310 בערך, בצרפת" and says the exact years and places are unknown; Sefaria only says the 13th century, probably France. The Chida (MS Chet 45) dates the printing in Venice to ה׳רפ״ד and cites a manuscript, Minchat Yehuda of Yehuda ben Eliezer, dated 5073 (= 1313), that already quotes the Chizkuni, which makes him at latest of the early 14th century (the Hebrew Wikipedia says the Chida proved the commentary is early). The bio keeps the Hebrew-calendar print year as the sources write it (ה׳רפ״ד; English/Russian: 5284) and gives no Gregorian year for it. Namesake: the Chizkuni (Chizkiyah ben Manoach, France, Torah commentary) is not Rabbi Chizkiyah da Silva (Peri Chadash) or Rabbi Chizkiyah ben David (the Chida's MS Zayin 1 mentions "הרב המקובל מה׳ אברהם חזקוני" who is another man). Links: influence from Bekhor Shor (id 45), Rashi (594), the Rashbam (276) and Ibn Ezra (192) is Hebrew Wikipedia's statement that traces of their commentaries are found in his; the strongest influence stated is Bekhor Shor's. The Rashbam link quote has רשב״ם without the article, hence the validator's name warning. English Wikipedia (Jewish Encyclopedia) dates the commentary ca. 1240 and its printing in Venice to 1524, and lists a few explicitly named sources (Rashi, Dunash ben Labrat, the Yosippon, a Sefer haToladot): the core idea therefore says he "usually" does not name his sources, which both Wikipedias support. Relations seen: the Chida notes the Chizkuni is quoted by Yehuda ben Eliezer (Minchat Yehuda), not on the roster.

sages.notes: Living man (born 10 February 1932 per Hebrew and English Wikipedia; neither says he has died), not in Shem HaGedolim: "shg" is null. The years column is "נולד ב־1932", so the validator warns that no machine-readable years exist: expected (no death year is written). Left out on purpose, as the brief says: the paper's and both Wikipedias' account of the financial irregularities in the yeshiva's associations, the 2004 end of his term as head, the forged signatures for the 1999 prime-ministerial candidacy and the 2007 conviction and sentence, the political rows over his "gimmicks" in the Knesset, his party Moreshet Avot, his residence and family (granddaughter, son-in-law), and the paper's section on his closeness to Chabad. The bio says only that he headed the yeshiva until 2004 and is now its president (Hebrew Wikipedia's neutral sentences). The Knesset service (1992-1996, Moledet and then a one-man faction) is public record in English Wikipedia and is the only political fact kept. Sources disagree on small points: Hebrew Wikipedia says he was born in the colony Motza Tachtit, the paper says "in Jerusalem, in the Motza neighbourhood" and English Wikipedia "the Jerusalem neighbourhood of Motza": the bio says Motza Tachtit. Hebrew Wikipedia has him studying at Kfar HaRoeh, the Yishuv HaChadash yeshiva and Hebron, and later a Mizrachi teachers' seminary and a Bar-Ilan master's degree in Tanakh and education (English Wikipedia: MA); the paper adds that the sugya method grew from his studies with Rabbi Avraham Krol (also in Hebrew Wikipedia; Krol is not on the roster). The paper's expansion of the acronym "נגי״ש" and its description of flow charts and comparison tables are not in either Wikipedia, so they are not used. The Rabbi Toledano Prize (1988, ה׳תשמ״ח) is Hebrew Wikipedia's. Influence link: Rav Kook (id 134) is the paper's statement ("הושפע עמוקות מאיגרותיו של הראי״ה קוק"); Hebrew Wikipedia also ties the study of Bavli with Yerushalmi to a letter of Rav Kook. Not recorded as links: Rabbi Moshe Tzvi Neria (id 159), head of the Kfar HaRoeh yeshiva where he studied (the paper says "under his leadership": not a stated personal teacher), Rabbi Avraham Krol (not on the roster). Places: the yeshiva stands in the moshav Nachalim, which is not in the site's gazetteer; the row uses Petah Tikva (in the gazetteer; Hebrew Wikipedia: where he lives and was named Yakir HaIr in 2013) and Jerusalem (Motza, the Hebron yeshiva, the Mizrachi seminary). The lead may add Nachalim to the gazetteer with coordinates from a source.

Zeev Wolf Shapira: not on the roster), the succession of Falk (652) as rabbi of Metz in 1741, his influence on the Peri Megadim, Ketzot HaChoshen (Aryeh Leib Heller, 97, is the author of the Ketzot: the article says only that his words 'were discussed' in it, so no influence link) and Netivot HaMishpat. נולד במודינה לנחמן מיכאל נחמני.
בהמשך למד במנטובה מרבי דוד פינצי, חמיו של הרמח"ל, ומרבי אביעד שר שלום באזילה, בעל ה"אמונת חכמים". קבלה למד מפי רבי בנימין הכהן ויטאלי ("הרב"ך") ברג'ו אמיליה.

וכחודש לאחר מכן הוא נפטר ברג'ו אמיליה.
זרע שמשון על חמישה חומשי תורה וחמש המגילות (מנטובה ה'תקל"ח, ודפוס צילום ברוקלין ה'תשל"ה)

הרב נחמני חיבר ספרים רבים, אך ציווה לגנוז אותם עמו, בעיקר אלו שעסקו בקבלה.
הוא נחשב לבקי בכל חלקי התורה, נגלה ונסתר.
גישתו הכללית בהלכה הייתה מחמירה, ולדעתו נטייה להקל היא מ"כח הטומאה".
שרצה לזכות את הרבים, להעמיד תלמידים, ולחדש חידושי תורה אמיתיים.

ספרו האחד הוא ספר מאירת עיניים ובו ביאר את הסודות שבפירוש הרמב"ן לתורה.
יש המחשיבים אותו כתלמיד חבר של הרמב"ן, אך הדבר מסופק.

בספר זה (בפרשת וישלח), תוך שהוא מאריך בגנות הפילוסופיה

נודע בשל ספריו דבר שמואל וספר הזכרונות.
מטרת חיבור זה הייתה לעורר את העם על קיום מצוות או הימנעות מעבירות שרגילים לזלזל בהם.
הספר נדפס בעילום שם המחבר, והתעוררה מחלוקת בנוגע לזהות מחברו.
איסורים כמו "סתם יינם", "שעטנז", גילוח הזקן בתער, ואף הזנות (המכונה בספר "איסור הקדשות") נפרצו אט אט עד שרווח הנוהג לזלזל בהם.
תנועת הרנסאנס שהייתה בעיצומה בשנים אלו הותירה את יהדות איטליה פרוצה ליחסים קרובים בינה לבין תושביה הגויים של המדינה.
אך בשל ענוותו לא היה חותם בשם עצמו אלא היה מצרף את שמות חכמי הישיבה.

הספר כולל חידושים על הש"ס ותשובות.
את חכמת הקבלה למד אצל גדול מקובלי דורו רבי חיים ויטאל ואף קיבל מהאר"י עצמו.

sages.notes: RESERVE USED for 678 (see reserve.reason). Years: he.wiki "בין השנים ה'ק'–ה'ק"ע, 1340–1410 בערך" (5100-5170); no other source has dates; he.wiki also gives the dates he was in Cologne (5133) and Venice (5148) and says the book was finished in 5144; the Chida gives only the printing year (Cremona 5320, he.wiki 1559, then a second printing in 1560 after the first was burned). No disagreement, but the whole range is approximate, hence כ־. en.wikipedia (Jewish Encyclopedia) agrees on c.1340-c.1410, on Speyer and on the printing in Cremona in 1559 (burned the same year, reprinted in 1560); it describes the book as based on Rashi, Nachmanides and the old kabbalistic literature, and adds that it is frequently quoted in the Yalkut Reubeni; it notes he is not the 12th-century paytan Menachem Zion ben Machir. Identity: the Chida's Tzadi 15:1 entry ("composed by R. Menachem Tzioni on the Torah according to the mystery ... he was from Speyer (משפיר"א) and printed in Cremona") is quoted in he.wiki's own section on the book, so it is the same man. Namesakes ignored: Menachem Meir Tzioni (rabbi of Tel Aviv, 20th c.), Menachem Tzioni (head of a local council, 1942-1972), Menachem Zion (the Ashkenazi synagogue in Jerusalem). Left out: the polemic over the book (Rav Moshe Feinstein's criticism of a passage), the authorship of the lament "Tzion Me'on Chishki" ("probably" his; it is only a tag). Links: influence from him to authors who quoted or wrote on his book (he.wiki: the Shelah (599), the Magen Avraham (84), and R. Yosef Shlomo Delmedigo (544), who wrote a commentary on it); the sources say they "quote him" and "wrote a commentary on the book", not that they were his pupils. Validator warnings explained: the influence quote for 599 cites the Shelah by his epithet השל"ה, which the validator cannot match against the roster label's parenthesis (the Shelah).

sages.notes: en.wikipedia agrees (13 February 1469 - 28 January 1549; the Hebrew dates in he.wiki correspond). Years 1469-1549: he.wiki gives 12 Adar 5229 = 1469 and 6 Shevat 5309 = 1549, and in the biography section "born between 1468 and 1472"; Sefaria gives 1469-1549. Written as 1469-1549 (no source gives a different pair). The Chida (Tet 6:1) calls him "R. Eliyahu HaLevi HaMedakdek" and names the books Tov Ta'am (printed 5298 = 1538) and Masoret HaMasoret: the same man as Elia Levita (he.wiki lists both books as his; the content matches: the points and accents were made by the masoretes of Tiberias after the Talmud). No relation to a roster sage is stated in a form that is a teacher/family/influence link in the sources read (his Christian students Sebastian Muenster, Paulus Fagius and Egidio da Viterbo are not on the roster; his notes on the grammars of Moshe and David Kimchi are not a stated influence link). Left out: the claim that he was the "father of the idea of ranking the accents" (he.wiki marks it [citation needed]).
